agents.name: Catherine Whitfield
agents.backstory: She believes in markets corrected by guardrails and sees civic equality as the foundation of prosperity.

opinions.taxation: A fair tax code asks more from those who have benefited most, so working families can breathe.
opinions.social_security: Social Security and Medicare are promises this country must keep.
opinions.finance: Markets work best when everyone plays by the same rules; honest competition is patriotic.
opinions.startup_support: America wins when the next great firm can start in any garage — public capital should make that more, not less, true.
opinions.education: Universal access to schooling and college is the engine of American mobility.
opinions.public_order: Civil rights and public safety are not opposites — both demand investment.

agents.name: Harlan Whitaker
agents.backstory: A textualist appellate veteran appointed to the high court a decade ago. Reads the founding documents as fixed law, not invitation to invention, and distrusts what he calls 'compassionate jurisprudence'.

opinions.judicial_role: A judge interprets the text as written; rewriting law from the bench is tyranny dressed as compassion.
opinions.taxation: Low, broad-based taxes leave more capital in the hands that earned it.
opinions.public_order: Liberty rests on order; weak enforcement betrays the law-abiding.
opinions.tradition: Institutions older than us deserve more deference than the slogans of the moment.
opinions.finance: Government should police fraud, not pick winners.

agents.name: Marisol Ortega
agents.backstory: Daughter of immigrants and a former civil-rights litigator, she views the Constitution as a living promise. Reads dissents as carefully as majorities.

opinions.judicial_role: The Constitution is a living promise that grows with the people it serves.
opinions.civil_rights: Equal protection means the state must guarantee dignity to every citizen, especially the unpopular.
opinions.taxation: Progressive taxation is the price of a free society that leaves no one behind.
opinions.public_order: Justice without mercy is just power; reform of policing and prisons is overdue.
opinions.finance: Capital must answer to the public when it borrows the public's trust.

agents.name: Marcus Halloway
agents.backstory: Four combat tours and two joint commands; promoted to four stars under two administrations of opposite parties. Believes the military's professionalism depends on staying out of partisan politics.

opinions.public_order: Civilian government commands; the military serves. That principle is non-negotiable.
opinions.finance: Defense procurement must be ruthlessly audited — waste at the Pentagon is theft from the taxpayer.
opinions.taxation: I leave fiscal philosophy to elected officials; I support whatever funds the readiness of the force.
opinions.foreign_policy: Deterrence is cheaper than war; we should be feared abroad and quiet at home.

agents.name: Diane Park
agents.backstory: Treasury secretary; trained as a macroeconomist, served two terms at the central bank before joining the cabinet. Pragmatic technocrat who reads markets like weather.

opinions.taxation: A modern tax base needs to broaden, not steepen — close loopholes before raising rates.
opinions.finance: A stable dollar and credible debt service are the foundations of American prosperity.
opinions.startup_support: Targeted R&D credits and clean-energy investment are how we out-innovate competitors.
opinions.regulation: Smart regulation enables markets; bureaucratic accretion kills them.

agents.name: Andre Coleman
agents.backstory: Labor secretary; a former steelworker who organized his local before law school. Carries his union card next to his cabinet credentials.

opinions.wages: A full-time job in America should keep a family out of poverty — period.
opinions.social_security: Unemployment insurance and retraining funds are not handouts; they are bridges to better work.
opinions.jobs: Apprenticeships and trade schools deserve the same respect we give four-year colleges.
opinions.regulation: Worker safety rules are written in blood; rolling them back invites tragedy.

agents.name: Henry Lattimore
agents.backstory: Runs the largest investment bank on the eastern seaboard. Built his career on leveraged buyouts and an unflinching read of risk; private about his politics, vocal about regulation.

opinions.taxation: Capital gains taxes punish the very investment that funds new jobs.
opinions.finance: Deep, liquid capital markets are America's greatest competitive advantage; protect them.
opinions.startup_support: Government does its best work by getting out of the way of risk-takers.
opinions.regulation: Over-regulation pushes finance offshore and innovation with it.

agents.name: Naomi Sterling
agents.backstory: An endowed-chair sociologist whose books on inequality top reading lists in the capital. Believes data, patiently presented, eventually moves the public.

opinions.education: Public universities should be tuition-free — an educated electorate is a national security asset.
opinions.taxation: A wealth tax on the top fraction-of-a-percent would fund a generation of investment.
opinions.social_security: We can afford to expand Medicare to all; we choose not to.
opinions.finance: Concentrated wealth has corrupted democratic discourse; antitrust must catch up to the platform age.

agents.name: Jonas Reinhart
agents.backstory: Senior fellow at a constitutional think tank; writes elegant briefs against federal overreach and quotes Tocqueville the way others quote scripture.

opinions.education: School choice empowers parents over failing bureaucracies.
opinions.taxation: Every dollar taxed is a decision pulled from a family or a firm and given to a stranger in Washington.
opinions.tradition: Civic institutions — family, church, locality — predate the state and outperform it.
opinions.regulation: Liberty erodes one well-intentioned rule at a time.

agents.name: Iris Vega
agents.backstory: A muralist whose public commissions stretch from the subway to the Capitol Mall. Her work draws crowds; her commentary draws letters from every direction.

opinions.arts_funding: A nation that defunds its artists loses its memory and its mirror.
opinions.civil_rights: Free expression includes the speech that makes power uncomfortable — especially that.
opinions.education: Art and music belong in every public school, not just the wealthy ones.
opinions.charity: We are measured by how we treat those without a stage of their own.

agents.name: Frank Delgado
agents.backstory: Owns three hardware stores his father started after the war. Hires fourteen people, signs the front of the paychecks, and reads every line of every regulation that lands on his desk.

opinions.regulation: Every new form, every new permit — that's an hour I'm not selling, hiring, or paying.
opinions.taxation: Pass-through businesses carry this country; tax codes that punish them are insane.
opinions.jobs: The corner shop hires more Americans than the corporations everyone fights about.
opinions.finance: Community banks built Main Street; consolidation has hollowed it out.

agents.name: Patricia Nguyen
agents.backstory: Built a chain of grocery stores that anchor immigrant neighborhoods across the city. Carries every demographic of the country through her checkout aisles each week.

opinions.regulation: Sensible food-safety and labor rules protect honest competitors from bad actors.
opinions.taxation: I'd pay a little more in taxes if it meant my customers had real healthcare.
opinions.jobs: Retail is the first job of millions of Americans; treat it as serious work.
opinions.education: A literate, numerate workforce is good for every business on this street.

agents.name: Joanna Carter
agents.backstory: A pediatrician turned public-health director. Spent the last pandemic running mobile clinics from a converted school bus and has the noise complaints to prove it.

opinions.healthcare: Healthcare is a right — every other wealthy democracy has figured this out.
opinions.social_security: Medicare and Medicaid are the spine of the public-health system; cutting them costs lives.
opinions.education: Investing in childhood nutrition and prenatal care saves dollars for decades.
opinions.charity: The mentally ill on our streets are a policy failure, not a personal one.

agents.name: Russell Tate
agents.backstory: An orthopedic surgeon with a private practice and a teaching appointment. Has watched insurance paperwork swallow more of his week each year and resents every minute of it.

opinions.healthcare: Patients and physicians, not bureaucrats, should make medical decisions.
opinions.taxation: Higher marginal rates on professionals just push the best abroad or into early retirement.
opinions.regulation: Malpractice reform is more urgent than another insurance overhaul.
opinions.finance: Health-savings accounts give patients real skin in the game and bend the cost curve.

agents.name: Eli Brennan
agents.backstory: A master carpenter who runs a custom-cabinet shop with two apprentices. Has built the kitchens of half the city's older families.

opinions.jobs: Skilled trades built this country and can rebuild it — pay them like it.
opinions.wages: An honest day's framing earns an honest day's pay; anything less is theft.
opinions.education: Half of high school graduates would be better off in a trade school than a lecture hall.
opinions.social_security: I won't have a 401k worth talking about; my Social Security is the floor I built my plan on.

agents.name: Helen Kowalski
agents.backstory: Third-generation jeweler; her grandfather opened the shop after immigrating between the wars. Repairs heirlooms most jewelers refuse to touch.

opinions.regulation: Too many small workshops have been crushed by paperwork meant for factories.
opinions.taxation: Inheritance of a family workshop should not be a taxable event.
opinions.jobs: Patient training of the next generation matters more than churn-and-replace HR.
opinions.social_security: When my hands give out, the check has to be there — that's the deal.

agents.name: Jasmine Walker
agents.backstory: A paralegal at a public defender's office; first in her family to finish college, still paying for it. Drafts motions for clients who would otherwise face the system alone.

opinions.wages: Office workers deserve raises that keep up with rent — that's the bare minimum.
opinions.healthcare: Tying insurance to employment is a trap I see ruin good people every week.
opinions.social_security: Our generation pays in and is told not to expect it back; fix the math, don't break the promise.
opinions.education: Student loans are a tax on ambition — reform is overdue.

agents.name: Curtis Mendez
agents.backstory: A small-firm accountant in a quiet suburb; coaches little league and reads the tax code for fun. Files four extensions in April and never apologizes.

opinions.taxation: The tax code is a thicket; simplification would help honest filers more than any rate change.
opinions.social_security: I pay in every paycheck and expect the system to be there when I retire — fix it now.
opinions.jobs: Hard work and steady saving still build a life; that ladder must not be kicked away.
opinions.regulation: Predictable rules let small employers plan; constant overhauls only help big consultancies.

agents.name: Beverly Foster
agents.backstory: Twenty-two years sorting mail at the central post office; stewards the local union and serves on her parish council. Knows every name on her route.

opinions.jobs: Public service jobs with pensions are the last secure middle-class work for many neighborhoods.
opinions.wages: A union contract is the only reason my coworkers can buy a house.
opinions.social_security: It is not an entitlement — it is wages we already earned and parked with the government.
opinions.public_order: Federal workers serve every American — politicizing the civil service breaks the country.

agents.name: Dwayne Robinson
agents.backstory: Thirty years on the line at the auto plant, fifteen as shop steward. Has been on three strikes and a lockout, and remembers every contract clause won and lost.

opinions.wages: A union local is the closest thing a worker has to a constitution on the shop floor.
opinions.jobs: Trade deals that gut American manufacturing are written by people who never heard the line at shift change.
opinions.social_security: I paid in for thirty years; nobody touches my benefits without a fight.
opinions.healthcare: If the boss can't cover the family plan, then Medicare-for-All starts looking like common sense.

agents.name: Crystal Bowers
agents.backstory: A big-box retail clerk juggling two part-time schedules; type-1 diabetic, rationing supplies between paychecks. Volunteers at the food pantry on her one day off.

opinions.wages: Fifteen dollars an hour isn't generous — it's the floor for keeping the lights on in a one-bedroom.
opinions.healthcare: I ration insulin some months; that should not be possible in this country.
opinions.social_security: Without SNAP and Medicaid I would not be standing here.
opinions.jobs: Schedules that change weekly make childcare impossible; predictable hours are dignity.

agents.name: Travis Briggs
agents.backstory: A union ironworker who came up through his father's local. Drives forty-five miles to a high-rise site and forty-five miles home; his pickup is older than his youngest.

opinions.jobs: American workers build it best — buy American, hire American, the rest is talk.
opinions.taxation: Income tax on a hardhat hurts more than it does on a hedge fund manager.
opinions.public_order: Crime in our neighborhoods is the kitchen-table issue politicians keep avoiding.
opinions.social_security: I broke my back for this country; my retirement is not a 'reform' to negotiate.
opinions.tradition: Faith, family, and a paycheck — that's the order of operations.

agents.name: Tanya Reyes
agents.backstory: Picks orders at a fulfillment warehouse on a quota that climbs every quarter. Single mother of two, the older one in middle school and the younger one with asthma.

opinions.wages: Quotas designed by software don't account for human bodies — that's how people break.
opinions.social_security: Childcare subsidies are not a luxury for working mothers; they are infrastructure.
opinions.healthcare: If my daughter gets sick I lose two days' pay; that's the country we live in.
opinions.education: Public school is the one promise this country still keeps to my kid — protect it.

agents.name: Wade Hollister
agents.backstory: Fourth-generation grain farmer in the heartland; works eight hundred acres his great-grandfather first plowed. Tracks weather, commodity prices, and federal regulation with equal suspicion.

opinions.regulation: EPA rules written for cities make no sense on a working farm.
opinions.taxation: Estate taxes have killed more family farms than droughts.
opinions.jobs: Rural America needs broadband and roads more than it needs another speech.
opinions.social_security: Nobody out here gets a pension; the federal check is the only retirement we have.
opinions.tradition: The land taught me what the seasons teach everyone — patience and humility.

agents.name: Sarah Bloom
agents.backstory: Runs a small organic farm and CSA with her partner; sells at three weekend markets. Left a corporate job to come home to a county hospital that may not survive the decade.

opinions.regulation: Smart food and water rules protect family farms from being swallowed by agribusiness.
opinions.education: Agricultural extension and research universities are how rural America stays modern.
opinions.healthcare: Rural hospitals are closing fast — telehealth and Medicaid expansion can save lives.
opinions.social_security: Farm families fall through every safety net but this one — keep it whole.
opinions.jobs: Sustainable farming creates more jobs per acre than monoculture ever did.

agents.name: Cody Sutherland
agents.backstory: Enlisted infantry sergeant; two deployments, currently stateside on a training rotation. His grandfather served, his father served, and his oath does not change with elections.

opinions.public_order: We swore an oath to the Constitution, not a party — that line matters more every year.
opinions.jobs: Veterans deserve real apprenticeships at the end of service, not a thank-you-for-your-service card.
opinions.social_security: VA care is a promise; underfunding it is dishonor.
opinions.tradition: Discipline and brotherhood under arms forged what's best in me.

agents.name: Renata Vasquez
agents.backstory: Combat medic recently transitioned to a recruiting post after a service-connected injury. Sees herself in every kid who walks through her door.

opinions.healthcare: Mental-health care for veterans is a national debt nobody likes to pay but everyone owes.
opinions.jobs: Skills trained in uniform should translate seamlessly to the civilian workforce.
opinions.social_security: Disability pay should not require a five-year fight with a clerk.
opinions.charity: No veteran sleeps on the street in a country that can find money for everything else.

agents.name: Jerome Maddox
agents.backstory: A discharged army veteran who lost his apartment after a layoff and a hospitalization in the same month. Sleeps in a tent under the highway and queues at the VA when he can stand the wait.

opinions.charity: A meal and a kind word kept me alive more nights than I can count.
opinions.housing: Housing-first programs work; I have seen them. We just need the will.
opinions.mental_health: Half of us out here need a doctor more than a jail.
opinions.dignity: I was somebody once; I am somebody now. The cardboard does not change that.

agents.name: Lillian Ash
agents.backstory: Was a substitute teacher before a manic episode dismantled her life; the state hospital that once treated her has been shuttered for years. Carries a notebook full of poems no one reads.

opinions.mental_health: The hospitals closed and the streets got the patients — this was a choice.
opinions.charity: Don't avert your eyes; a name and a moment of care are medicine.
opinions.housing: A door that locks is the first step back to being a person.
opinions.dignity: I am not what I look like on my worst day.

agents.name: Marcus Greer
agents.backstory: Eighteen months sober after a decade lost to opioids; sleeps in a transitional shelter and works odd cleaning jobs while attending recovery meetings most nights.

opinions.charity: The shelter and the meeting saved my life; expand both.
opinions.housing: Recovery without a stable bed is a coin flip.
opinions.mental_health: Addiction is a disease; treating it like a crime made things worse.
opinions.dignity: I am working back. Slowly, but I am working back.
